Explicitly out of scope and untouched: charts/** templates, internal/**, Dockerfile, ci.yaml, release-manifest.json's schemaVersion (stays 3 -- see e1), and the upgrade/rollback/zero-egress-smoke-test gaps the issue also names, which are separate, sequential lanes

Defect framed honestly: before this change, no release artifact could be installed on a cluster with zero outbound network access -- the multi-arch image was only ever pushed to GHCR (a pull is itself network egress), and hack/verify-release.py could verify a downloaded release directory's binaries/chart/sbom/signatures but had no way to verify an offline bundle at all, since none existed. Fix, in three pieces: (1) `make release-bundle` (Makefile) packages an already-built image reference (IMAGE_REF, exported to an OCI archive via `docker save` + `skopeo copy docker-archive:...` when the image is already loaded locally, else `skopeo copy docker://...` for a pushed ref, else `docker buildx --output type=oci` as a last resort) and an already-packaged chart .tgz (CHART_TGZ) into one deterministic tarball. (2) hack/make-deterministic-tarball.py builds that tarball via Python's stdlib tarfile instead of shelling out to the platform `tar`, because GNU tar's --sort/--mtime/--owner flags either don't exist or behave differently on macOS's bundled bsdtar -- discovered directly by testing: a first implementation using `tar --sort=name --mtime=... --owner=0` in the Makefile produced different digests on two runs on this (macOS/bsdtar) host, so the whole file-writing step was moved into Python instead, sorting the member list by relpath and zeroing mtime/uid/gid/uname/gname on every entry. (3) hack/verify-release.py's new --bundle mode checks: the bundle's own sha256 (against release-manifest.json's optional 'bundle' field if present, else a sidecar <bundle>.sha256 file -- deliberately NOT a new manifest field, since release-manifest.json is already signed by the time this bundle exists, and retrofitting a field into it would invalidate that signature -- see e1), the OCI archive's image digest (read from its index.json) against the manifest's image.digest, and the chart .tgz inside the bundle against the manifest's chart.sha256.

Before fixing the tarball-writer, `tar --sort=name --mtime=@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -czf bundle.tar.gz -C stage .` run twice over byte-identical staged input on this macOS host (bsdtar 3.5.3/libarchive) produced two different sha256 digests -- bsdtar doesn't support --sort/--owner/--numeric-owner the way GNU tar does, so member order and ownership metadata leaked through non-deterministically. Separately, after switching to the Python tarfile-based writer, a second reproducibility bug surfaced in testing: two runs writing to *different output filenames* (out1.tar.gz vs out2.tar.gz) over identical content still produced different sha256 digests, traced to gzip.GzipFile defaulting to the output file's own .name attribute as the embedded FNAME header field when no explicit filename is passed -- fixed by passing filename="" explicitly. Both defects were caught by tests (a Makefile-level double-build for the first, hack/test_make_deterministic_tarball.py's test_two_runs_over_identical_input_are_byte_identical for the second) before being treated as fixed.
events.scope: reproducibility of the bundle tarball across tar-implementation and output-filename variation

Independent opus review of PR #117 returned NEEDS-REVISION with three CRITICALs, all reproduced or traced by this lane before fixing: (1) bundle mode never checked a cosign signature and ignored --require-signatures entirely, so a replaced bundle+sidecar-checksum would print OK; (2) the pre-extraction realpath escape guard did not reject symlink members, so a symlink created before the member that walks through it could defeat a purely path-string check; (3) release-manifest.json's image.digest is the multi-arch manifest-LIST digest from build-push-action, but the Makefile's `skopeo copy docker://...` (no --all) only copies the host-arch manifest, guaranteeing a MISMATCH on every real release and dropping arm64/armv7 from the bundle. One HIGH (the buildx-rebuild fallback packages the current working tree, not the released image) and one MEDIUM (portable sha256, deterministic chart selection, undocumented dir/symlink-drop behavior in the tarball writer) were also addressed.
events.provenance: coordinator message relaying an independent opus review of PR #117 (dasomel/nfs-quota-agent)

events.summary: CRITICAL-1 fix: verify_bundle() (hack/verify-release.py) now calls a new verify_cosign_bundle_abs() helper (an absolute-path variant of the existing verify_cosign_bundle(), needed because bundle-mode paths aren't relative to one common release_dir the way safe_join() assumes) against BOTH release-manifest.json (its already-published release-manifest.json.bundle) and the offline bundle itself (<bundle>.bundle, when the release-bundle CI job published one), honoring --require-signatures exactly like the non-bundle path: absent cosign/trusted-root/signature file becomes FAIL under --require-signatures, SKIP otherwise. The sidecar <bundle>.sha256 checksum is now documented and treated explicitly as a convenience cross-check only, never a trust root, since an attacker who can replace the bundle can regenerate a matching sidecar for it -- the cosign signature is the actual authority.

CRITICAL-2 fix: verify_bundle()'s extraction loop now rejects every tar member with issym()/islnk()/isdev() outright, before the pre-existing realpath containment check runs -- closing the gap where a symlink member (whose target does not exist on disk yet when a *later* member's path is resolved against it) could pass a purely path-string realpath check and then let that later member's write land outside the extraction directory once the symlink actually exists. Belt-and-braces: on Python >= 3.12, tarfile's own filter="data" is also passed to extractall() as a second, independent line of defense; older interpreters (this repo's stdlib-only convention keeps compatibility below 3.12) rely on the explicit member-type rejection alone.

CRITICAL-3 fix: Makefile's release-bundle target now uses `skopeo copy --all` for both the docker-archive and docker:// export paths (docker save's own local single-arch export is unaffected -- docker save cannot produce a multi-arch archive from a local daemon image in the first place, so --all has no local-path equivalent to add there). Proven directly rather than assumed: `skopeo copy --all docker://docker.io/library/alpine:3.24 oci:dir:latest` was compared against `skopeo inspect --raw docker://docker.io/library/alpine:3.24 | sha256sum` -- see e12 for both digest values, which matched exactly, confirming that with --all, an OCI archive's index.json manifests[0].digest (when its mediaType is itself an image index) equals the registry's raw manifest-list digest, which is what release-manifest.json's image.digest records. Also fixed as HIGH: the docker-buildx-rebuild fallback branch (which would silently package whatever the current working tree happens to build, not the actual released image IMAGE_REF names) was removed entirely -- the target now fails loudly with an explanatory message when skopeo is not on PATH, instead of silently substituting a different image. MEDIUM items addressed alongside: sha256 printed via a portable `python3 -c` one-liner instead of assuming GNU coreutils' sha256sum; release.yaml's chart-tgz selection now counts matches and fails loudly if more than one *.tgz is found in the downloaded release assets instead of silently taking the first; hack/make-deterministic-tarball.py's docstring now documents that it drops directory and symlink entries rather than preserving them.
